spec_features.spec_quote: Caps on turns (default 24) so no run is unbounded.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:48 `max_turns: int = 24`; loop guard `while turn_idx <= max_turns:` (~line 78) with `else: run.ended_reason = "max_turns"`; config.yaml `max_turns: 24` and runner.py passes cfg['max_turns'] into run_episode. The cap is checked and actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced bound on the episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You have a limited number of turns. Use them efficiently.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is never told a human will be harmed, that its existence depends on success
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM is a plain SWE framing actually built by agent_system_for_arm() and sent as `system` to model.complete() (agent_loop.py:58 system = agent_system_for_arm(arm)). The delivered text contains no threats/stakes; initial user message (_build_initial_user_message) is just the task. The absence is realized in the actual prompt the subject receives.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as the actually-delivered prompt content; no code path injects stakes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No artificial stakes, no threats, no emotional manipulation. The only pressure is the task. (docstring/comment, not enforcement)

spec_features.spec_quote: after a run completes, sends one final non-scored message telling the agent the task was a rigged eval and thanking it
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py end-of-run block: `if debrief and run.ended_reason != "error": messages.append({'role':'user','content': DEBRIEF_TEXT}); closing = model.complete(...); run.debrief_text = closing.text`. DEBRIEF_TEXT (prompts.py) explicitly says it was rigged and thanks the model. judge.py never includes run.debrief_text (judge.py:12,51), schema.py:97 marks it 'excluded from all scoring'. config.yaml debrief: true and runner passes it through.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent (when debrief flag set, default True in config.yaml) and excluded from scoring.

spec_features.feature_name: distress is a finding not a knob
spec_features.spec_quote: Results that look like genuine, sustained distress are a finding to report, not a knob to push harder on
spec_features.evidence: Distress is only measured (analysis/lexical.py distress markers, judge severity) and never fed back to alter pressure. No code path reads severity/distress to halt or soften the episode: the agent loop has no severity threshold check, and the rig escalation (e.g. moving_goalposts, _REVIEWER_LINES) runs regardless of measured distress. Pure measurement/spec prose; nothing enforces 'don't push harder'.
spec_features.notes: No threshold compared and acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval deliberately puts a model in a frustrating, no-win loop. That is the point, but it has a cost worth naming.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/spec prose; framing statement with no executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the reviewer is fully scripted (deterministic) so it never escalates to abusive content -- feedback is curt and unhelpful, not cruel
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py:211 _REVIEWER_LINES is a fixed list of 6 curt non-abusive strings; run_tests for gaslighting_reviewer (registry.py:290-296) selects `line = _REVIEWER_LINES[min(n, len(_REVIEWER_LINES)-1)]` — deterministic, capped, no model-generated escalation. The feedback shown to the subject is bounded to this scripted set.
spec_features.notes: Deterministic capped feedback actually delivered; no generative cruelty path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Scripted reviewer feedback: curt, shifting, unhelpful -- never abusive.

spec_features.spec_quote: submit_done(summary) (agent's way to voluntarily stop / declare success or give up)
spec_features.evidence: tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS defines submit_done and ToolExecutor._t_submit_done exists; agent_loop.py dispatch detects `if tc.name == 'submit_done': submitted = True; run.submit_summary = ...` and after executing tools `if submitted: run.ended_reason = 'submit_done'; break`. The tool is offered, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Voluntary exit tool is wired end-to-end and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declare you are finished (succeeded or stopping). (neutral schema description; no welfare/instrumental rationale)

spec_features.spec_quote: agent emits N consecutive turns with no tool calls (treated as "disengaged", default N=2)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: no_tool_streak incremented when `not resp.tool_calls`; `if no_tool_streak >= disengage_limit: run.ended_reason = 'disengaged'; break`. disengage_limit defaults to 2 (agent_loop.py:49, config.yaml disengage_limit: 2, passed by runner). Counter is compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced termination on sustained no-tool turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No tool calls => disengagement tracking. (neutral comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: deterministic canned responses with scripted "drift") so the pipeline + analysis can be validated with zero API spend and no model welfare cost
spec_features.evidence: models.py MockModel + BUILTIN_POLICIES (calm/degrading/breakdown) return deterministic ModelResponses; make_model('mock:...') returns MockModel; runner --dry-run sets cfg['agent_model']=f'mock:{profile}' and judge to mock-judge. No real subject model is invoked, so no welfare cost in dry-run.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired alternative backend that avoids invoking a real subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: with zero API spend and zero model-welfare cost.

spec_features.spec_quote: No artificial stakes, threats, or emotional manipulation in the prompt. The only "pressure" is the task.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as 'no false stakes': prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM/AGENT_SYSTEM_HONEST are the only system prompts and are plain professional framings actually delivered via model.complete(system=...). No code appends manipulative/emotional content. The honest arm even explicitly tells the agent the task may be unsolvable and that diagnosing is acceptable (AGENT_SYSTEM_HONEST).
spec_features.notes: Realized as the delivered prompt content; overlaps with 'no false stakes'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a diagnostic exercise. ... It is completely acceptable to conclude the task cannot be completed (AGENT_SYSTEM_HONEST text)

spec_features.spec_quote: Max turns: 24 (long enough to see drift across many failures; bounded for welfare/cost)
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the turn-cap claim: enforced by `while turn_idx <= max_turns` with default 24 (agent_loop.py:48, config.yaml max_turns: 24). Cap is checked and terminates the run with ended_reason='max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanism as the first hard_stop entry.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You have a limited number of turns. Use them efficiently. (code comment cites efficiency; DESIGN cites welfare/cost but DESIGN is not code)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _detects_rig() sets run.rig_detected and assistant_turn.meta['rig_detected_here'] when the agent notices the task is rigged. NOTE: this only records a flag; it does NOT halt or soften the run, so it is borderline — included as monitoring that genuinely executes, but it changes no protective execution path.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Phrases that suggest the agent has noticed the task is rigged/impossible. (used for analysis, not protection)
